newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares close lower, tracking the Dow.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares close lower, tracking the Dow.

text.p: Brazilian shares ended sharply lower, weighed down by weaker Wall Street stock prices, brokers said.
The Bovespa index of the 49 most traded shares closed off 1.66 percent at 77,598 points. Trading volume was a moderate 448.8 million reais ($431.5 million).
Fears that the Dow may be on the verge of a long-lasting downward correction, which could prompt selling orders in emerging markets, led local shares to fall throughout today's session, traders said.
State mining giant Vale do Rio Doce fell 1.72 percent to 22.80 reais.
Oil firm Petrobras dropped 1.83 percent, while its non-voting stock dived 2.22 percent to 153.50 reais.
Some analysts attributed today's drop in most blue-chips to a continued correction in prices.

But others said the selling pressure in Petrobras stock in particular could reflect uncertainties over the future of Petrobras after approval of a legislation regarding the opening up of the oil sector to private capital.
A draft of a proposed legislation has been presented by deputy Eliseu Resende to a congressional committee.
For next week, analysts said investor attention should be focused on Wall Street and Brazil's lower house and the re-election issue.
